  1. ✦

    Love:

    Love & Compatibility

    The pattern underneath who you are drawn to is steadier than the people themselves. You go towards the ones who move at your speed and stay with the ones who slow you down, which is a costly way round — and it is worth knowing before the next one.

    • Your sign + a fire signWORKS

      Pace matches, and neither of you waits for the other to finish deciding. How to play it: say the quiet part in the first week rather than the fourth — this one rewards being told, and reads a pause as a verdict.

    • Your sign + an earth signWORKS

      They hold the ground you move across, and the holding is easy to stop seeing. How to play it: name one specific thing they carried, out loud, every week — steady people leave when the steadiness goes unread.

    • Your sign + a mirror of yourselfAVOID

      Two of the same energy make a fast start and a short middle, and nothing in the pairing slows anything down. How to protect your energy: keep one thing in your week that is yours alone and do not move it for them.

    • Your sign + somebody who needs managingAVOID

      You are good at carrying, which is exactly why this one costs you more than it costs them. How to protect your energy: stop offering before you are asked, once, and watch what they do with the gap.

    In the first month ask the second question rather than the first — the answer to that one tells you something.

  3. ✦

    Blind spots:

    5 Hidden Strengths & Blind Spots

    1. 1

      You wait for the perfect moment to say it

      You take in more than anyone in the room and hold it longer, which is why your read is almost always right. It is also why it arrives after the situation has resolved without you in it.

      → Set a three-day ceiling between noticing something and naming it, clumsy wording included.

    2. 2

      You read your own certainty as evidence

      A Deep Water profile decides quickly and trusts the speed of it. A decision made out of restlessness feels identical, from the inside, to one made out of conviction.

      → Sleep one night on any decision you could explain in ten seconds.

    3. 3

      You hold the useful thing until the moment is clean

      You notice more than the people around you and you say less of it. The read is usually right and it usually arrives late, by which point the situation has resolved without you in it.

      → Set a ceiling of three days between noticing something and naming it, clumsy wording included.

    4. 4

      You absorb the cost rather than name it

      You take the extra hour and the awkward conversation, and you take them quietly enough that nobody learns they were extra. Over a few years the baseline moves.

      → Say what it took, once, at the moment it happens, without asking for anything back.

    5. 5

      You leave at the point it stops being interesting

      You see the shape of a thing early, which is the hard part. Once the shape is clear the rest reads as admin, and the value gets collected by whoever stayed.

      → Pick one thing a quarter and stay past the boredom.

  4. ✦

    Blueprint:

    Your Cosmic Blueprint

    A Deep Water blueprint runs on three things at once: the element you return to under pressure, the energy you keep time by, and the tone other people read first. Most of the time the three agree, and while they do you are easy to be around and easy to read for yourself.

    The interesting part is where they pull against each other. The tone arrives before the element does, so people meet the surface and adjust to it, and a certain amount of every week goes on correcting an impression you did not set out to make.

    • You decide faster than you can explain, which is worth trusting and worth writing down.
    • Rest that looks like doing nothing does not restore you; rest with a shape does.
    • People read your tone as your whole position, so the thing you say lightly is the thing they carry away.
  5. ✦

    Money:

    Career & Money Path

    Work with a visible edge and a short feedback loop

    A Deep Water energy earns where the result comes back quickly enough to steer by, and drifts on long horizons with no signal. Three moves: put the hardest thing in the first two hours of your day, before the room fills; ask for a check-in at the halfway point of anything longer than a month; and work the two days either side of a deadline rather than the week before it.

    Where to stop spending it

    • Work that needs performing The energy it takes to be a version of yourself all day is energy not spent on the work itself. Decline it by asking what the output is — if the answer is a presence, it is not work.
    • Roles built entirely on maintaining You will do it well, and it will cost you more than it costs somebody suited to it. Decline it by naming the part you will hold and the part you will hand back.
    • Anything measured only in hours It rewards presence over judgement, and judgement is the thing you actually have. Put a deliverable on it before you agree, or let it go to somebody who is paid to sit there.

    The leak is the second half of your afternoon, given away in pieces to things that arrived rather than things you chose. Plug it by booking the last ninety minutes of the day to yourself before anyone else books them, and treating that block as unmovable.
